pillars.title: A tracker that doesn't pretend
pillars.subtitle: Most apps show one confident date and hope for the best. Bodies vary, so this one shows you how sure it is, in plain language.

honest.text: See the days your period will most likely start and how likely that is. The range gets tighter as you log more cycles.

privacy.title: Your cycle is your business
privacy.text: Period data is some of the most personal data there is. This app is built around that, not bolted on afterwards.
privacy.p1: No ads, no analytics, no third-party trackers
privacy.p2: Your data is never sold or handed over to advertisers
privacy.p3: Every share link is opt-in and can be reset or switched off
privacy.p4: Delete your account and all your data whenever you like
privacy.selfText: The code is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence. Run your own copy with Docker, on Railway or on Kubernetes: your server, your data.

free.a: Yes. There is no paid plan, no ads and no data selling. Because the code is open source, you can also run your own copy.

accuracy.a: Every forecast comes with a range and a stated chance, like “80% likely between 10 and 14 Nov”. The more cycles you log, the better it knows you. The forecast has been tested on simulated cycles, not on real people's data, so instead of big accuracy promises you get the uncertainty, shown plainly.

irregular.q: What if my cycles are irregular?
irregular.a: That's fine. The forecast learns your own pattern and shows a wider range when your cycles vary more. If a period is late, it says so instead of quietly moving the date.

contraception.q: Can I use it as birth control?
contraception.a: No. The fertile window is a calendar estimate. It isn't contraception or conception advice.

data.a: Only you, unless you create a share link. Partner and calendar links show only what you choose, and you can reset or stop them at any time.

phone.q: Does it work on my phone?
phone.a: Yes. It runs in any modern browser, and you can add it to your home screen on iPhone and Android so it opens like an app.

cta.subtitle: Sign up in under a minute and log when your last period started. Your forecast gets sharper with every cycle.

google.title: Google Calendar
google.steps: On a computer, open Google Calendar. Next to “Other calendars” press +, choose “From URL”, paste the link and press “Add calendar”.

apple.title: iPhone, iPad, Mac
apple.steps: iPhone: Settings, Calendar, Accounts, Add Account, Other, Add Subscribed Calendar, paste the link. Mac: Calendar app, File, New Calendar Subscription.

outlook.title: Outlook
outlook.steps: Open Outlook on the web. Choose Add calendar, then “Subscribe from web”, paste the link and give it a name.

how.delay: Calendar apps refresh subscribed calendars every few hours, so changes can take a while to show up.
